_comment: Conventional Commits → a version bump, a tag, and a GitHub Release.
── One package, one version
sheng ships a single crate, published to crates.io only — no Python
bindings, no second manifest. `Cargo.toml`'s `[package] version` is the
only mirror, and it carries the `x-release-please-version` marker below.
── Why `simple` + generic extra-files
`simple` keeps the manifest as the source of truth; the `generic` updater
rewrites the semver on any line carrying an `x-release-please-version`
annotation. `tools/version_parity.py`'s successor — the shared
`package-release version` command — fails if a marked line is missing
from this list, so the two cannot drift apart.
── Changelog ownership
towncrier owns CHANGELOG.md — the curated fragments under changelog.d/ are
the release notes, written for people. release-please would compile a
second, machine-derived changelog into the same file and fight it, so
`skip-changelog` is on and the bot handles versions and tags only. The
`fold changelog` job in release-please.yml builds the notes and commits
them onto this PR's branch automatically; release.yml's preflight
re-checks that the fold landed before it will publish anything.
── The tag cascades
Merging the release PR tags `vX.Y.Z`, which is what `release.yml` waits
for to publish the crate. A tag pushed by GITHUB_TOKEN does NOT trigger
another workflow, so that hand-off only happens because release-please runs
as the `billy-company-release` GitHub App rather than as Actions — see
.github/workflows/release-please.yml.
